# AX310 wire specification

**Generated by `ax310_spec` from `src/ax310/Protocol.hpp` and `src/ax310/Types.hpp`. Do not edit.**

Every address, length, offset, range, default and name below is read from the constant that implements it, so none of them can disagree with the driver. `ctest -R wire-specification` fails when this file and the headers have parted; `ax310_spec --write docs/wire-protocol.md` brings them back together.

The sentences around the tables are prose, and prose is what drifts. Where one makes a claim a table cannot hold -- an endianness, an ordering, a range -- there is a test in `Protocol_test.cpp` that fails if it stops being true. Those are tagged `[spec]`.

What is *not* here is the evidence. Why a register is believed to mean what it means, which readings were wrong first, and what remains unknown live in `AGENT.md` and `.agent/rules/`, because none of that is derivable from a table.

## The two USB devices

One physical unit enumerates as two devices at once, not as two states of one. Only the control device carries the deck's protocol.

| Mode | Product id | HID interface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | `0x0310` | 4 |
| Control | `0x1310` | 0 |

## The input report

58 bytes, or 64 when padded. hidapi prepends the report id for a device that numbers its reports and not for one that does not, so both lengths arrive; `protocol::reportPayload()` is the one place that decides which.

The report is **mixed-endian**: touch coordinates are little-endian and the audio meters are big-endian, in the same frame.

| Offset | Field |
| --- | --- |
| `0x00` | event type; `0x10` is a screen touch. The button bitmask on any other report. |
| `0x01` | touch flags — seven values seen, meaning unknown |
| `0x02` | touch x, little-endian |
| `0x04` | touch y, little-endian |
| `0x06` | knob push bitmask |
| `0x07` | knob capacitive-touch bitmask |
| `0x08` | knob rotation counters, 6 of them, relative rather than positions |
| `0x12` | audio meters: 6 tracks × 4 bytes — a left and a right, both 16-bit big-endian, full scale `0x7fff` |
| `0x39` | checksum |

The meters are one per track in the deck's printed knob order, and the deck sends all 6 of them on every report.

### Bit masks

| Button | Bit |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `0x08` |
| 2 | `0x04` |
| 3 | `0x02` |
| 4 | `0x01` |

| Knob | Bit |
| --- | --- |
| Mic | `0x01` |
| Line In | `0x02` |
| Console | `0x04` |
| System | `0x08` |
| Game | `0x10` |
| Chat | `0x20` |

## Property registers

A byte-addressed register space, reached with a feature report of `[0x01|0x81] 0x10 <address> <length> <values…>` — set and get. A reply carries the kind at byte 1, the group at 2, the address at 3, the length at 4 and the values from 5.

| Address | Name | Preserved on connect | Writable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x0f` | DisplayPower | no | yes |
| `0x14` | KnobLedModeAt14 | yes, 1 byte | yes |
| `0x15` | SelectedMix (00 creator, 01 audience) | yes, 1 byte | yes |
| `0x1d` | SettingsTransaction (01 begin, 00 end) | no | yes |
| `0x1e` | KnobLedBrightness | yes, 1 byte | yes |
| `0x21` | KnobLedSelect / mixer mode | yes, 1 byte | yes |
| `0x27` | creator mix levels (base; +track) | yes, 7 bytes | yes |
| `0x2a` | creator System level | no | yes |
| `0x2b` | creator Game level | no | yes |
| `0x2c` | creator Chat level | no | yes |
| `0x2e` | audience mix levels (base; +track) | no | yes |
| `0x31` | audience System level | no | yes |
| `0x35` | KnobPropertyAt35 | yes, 1 byte | yes |

13 addresses are read before the handshake and written back after it, because the captured init sequence is somebody's saved configuration rather than an initialisation. The longest is 7 bytes.

Writes are refused to: `0x16` — writing there once wedged a deck badly enough to need a power cycle.

### Per-track levels

Two contiguous blocks of 6 bytes, one per mix, addressed `base + track` in knob order. A level is 20 steps and one step is exactly 5%.

| Mix | Base | Mic | Line In | Console | System | Game | Chat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Creator | `0x27` | `0x27` | `0x28` | `0x29` | `0x2a` | `0x2b` | `0x2c` |
| Audience | `0x2e` | `0x2e` | `0x2f` | `0x30` | `0x31` | `0x32` | `0x33` |

## Framed commands

The DSP chain uses a second family: `0xfe 0x00 <length> <command> <body…> <checksum>`, 5 bytes of overhead around a body of at most 22.

| Command | Name |
| --- | --- |
| `0x85` | DelayEffectEnable (reverb/echo) |
| `0x87` | EqualiserEnableA |
| `0x88` | EqualiserEnableB |
| `0x94` | DelayEffectParameters (byte 14: 1 reverb, 2 echo) |
| `0x9c` | EqualiserEnableC |
| `0x9e` | NoiseGateParameters |
| `0x9b` | CompressorEnable |
| `0x9f` | CompressorParameters |
| `0xa3` | EqualiserBand |
| `0xb2` | Commit |

### Parameters

7 of them, each one row of `protocol::Parameters`. A parameter located later becomes one more row and appears in both interfaces with no other change.

| Effect | Parameter | Command | Body offset | Encoding | Range | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reverb | Level | `0x94` | 3 | unsigned byte | 0…255 | — |
| Reverb | Decay | `0x94` | 1 | unsigned byte | 0…255 | — |
| Reverb | Damp | `0x94` | 2 | unsigned byte | 0…255 | — |
| Reverb | Diffusion | `0x94` | 8 | unsigned byte | 0…255 | — |
| Reverb | Room size | `0x94` | 18 | unsigned 16, little-endian | 0…1023 | — |
| Compressor | Threshold | `0x9f` | 9 | signed byte | -60…0 | dB |
| Compressor | Ratio | `0x9f` | 11 | unsigned byte | 1…20 | :1 |

The DSP chain has no read-back, so the driver keeps a known-good body per parameterised command and edits it in place. 2 such bodies are held.

- `0x94` (DelayEffectParameters (byte 14: 1 reverb, 2 echo)), 21 bytes: `40` `9b` `ff` `19` `40` `7f` `80` `66` `e5` `10` `00` `4e` `04` `40` `01` `43` `05` `ff` `ca` `00` `10`
- `0x9f` (CompressorParameters), 17 bytes: `00` `a0` `00` `10` `83` `0e` `83` `0e` `00` `ee` `00` `0c` `d6` `04` `31` `00` `1f`

## The screen

JPEG frames go out on the output endpoint in chunks of 1025 bytes: a 13-byte header and 1012 bytes of payload.

| Offset | Field |
| --- | --- |
| `0x01` | sequence number |
| `0x02` | 2 bytes marking the last chunk of a frame — `0x01` on the final chunk, `0x00` on every other |
| `0x09` | payload length, little-endian |
| `0x0b` | payload sum, little-endian — the 16-bit unsigned sum of the chunk's payload bytes |

Without the final-chunk marker the deck accepts every chunk, reports no error and never puts the frame on screen.

## Knob LED rings

A knob property is 7 bytes, with the ring level at offset 4, 20 at full. The captured init sequence sets brightness `0x0d`.
